standard_prerequisites.name: Homotopy fibres of the total map
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a fiberwise transformation between two families over a type, the homotopy fibre of the total map at a point is equivalent to the homotopy fibre of the fiberwise map at the second component, so contractibility transfers.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the pointwise input of the proof, cited by the retained text.

standard_prerequisites.name: Fiberwise equivalence as pointwise contractibility
standard_prerequisites.statement: A fiberwise transformation is a fiberwise equivalence exactly when each of its homotopy fibres is contractible, and a total map is an equivalence exactly when each of its homotopy fibres is contractible.
standard_prerequisites.use: It converts the pointwise statement about contractible fibres into the equivalence of the two maps.

core_obligations: Fix the fiberwise transformation and the two families as in the statement (source line 774).

Use the cited lemma to obtain, for every point of the base and every point of the target family, that the homotopy fibre of the total map and the homotopy fibre of the fiberwise map at those points are contractible under the same condition (source lines 775-778).

Convert the resulting pointwise equivalence into the stated equivalence of the two maps: the total fibres range over all points of the total space exactly as the pointwise fibres range over all points of the base together with all points of their fibres (source line 779).

proof_roadmap.step: Pointwise contractibility of the two kinds of homotopy fibre.
Regroup the pointwise statement into the equivalence of the total map.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled theorem at source lines 767-771: a fiberwise transformation is a fiberwise equivalence exactly when its total map is an equivalence. The proof (source lines 773-780) carries out the regrouping that is not visible in the statement: it first invokes the cited comparison of the two kinds of homotopy fibre to obtain contractibility of the fibre of the total map at a point if and only if the pointwise fibre is contractible, and then observes that ranging over all points of the total space is the same as first ranging over the base and then over each fibre, which turns the pointwise equivalence into the equivalence of the two maps. The regrouping of the quantifiers is the substance of the card.
